item.title: Instagram Head Adam Mosseri Addresses AI Negativity, Ranking, and Account Labeling
item.description:
Instagram Head Adam Mosseri Addresses AI Negativity, Ranking, and Account Labeling

In an interview on the Colin and Samir podcast, Instagram head Adam Mosseri addressed growing anxiety surrounding artificial intelligence, discussing creator concerns, platform ranking, and Instagram’s policies on AI-generated content.

🔍 Overview

Mosseri acknowledged that negativity surrounding AI is “going to get worse” and will continue to intensify over the next couple of years, particularly across creative industries. He noted that while some frustration and anger is founded and some unfounded, the underlying sentiment across various fields comes down to “a fear of being left behind in some way.”

⚙️ Content Ranking and Policies

Mosseri detailed how Instagram approaches AI-generated material and profiles on the platform:

  • AI Ranking Quality: Instagram does not rank AI creators differently, but Mosseri indicated the platform likely does not rank AI content as well as non-AI content due to quality variations. He noted there is both “great AI content” and “AI slop,” though he believes the term “slop” is used “too liberally.”
  • No Banning Strategy: Instagram is actively working on solutions for misleading AI content like celebrity deepfakes, but Mosseri stated, “I don’t think it’s practical for us to try and ban AI content from the platform.”
  • Account Labeling: Following an initial label launch earlier this year and a crackdown on AI-generated profiles in August, Instagram is starting to require AI accounts to label themselves so users can distinguish between real and un-real content.

💡 Key Concerns Identified

During the interview, Mosseri outlined specific fears expressed by creators and professionals:

  • Content Rights: Concerns over creators owning their content and models being trained on that content.
  • Safety and Displacement: Fears regarding platform safety and job displacement affecting content creators, engineers, and mathematicians.

#Instagram #Meta #GenerativeAI #SocialMedia #AIContent

Source: Adam Mosseri says negativity around AI is ‘going to get worse’

item.title: Meta pauses Muse chat-sharing feature after security leak
item.description:
Meta pauses Muse chat-sharing feature after security leak

Meta has temporarily disabled the Muse sharing feature that let users generate a public link to an AI conversation after researchers uncovered thousands of publicly discoverable links.

🔍 Overview

  • Researchers at security firm Claroc reported more than 6,800 Muse links exposed through public DNS records.
  • The exposure included sensitive data such as a marketing company’s revenue review, a small‑business loan application, a workplace full‑year staff calendar, and interview notes for an AI‑lab candidate.
  • In response, Meta paused the sharing functionality while it reviews the report.

🧩 How it works

  • Muse allowed users to “share specific Muse artifacts, which creates a page that can be accessed by those with the link,” according to spokesperson Tracy Clayton.
  • Each shared page’s URL was built from the conversation’s title, a short descriptive phrase, and a random ID.
  • The hostname often revealed the content type, and because the link contained the same title and ID, a hostname pulled from DNS could be used to reconstruct the full URL.

⚙️ Key details

  • Discovery method: Claroc searched public DNS records, which act as a directory for web traffic, to rebuild links.
  • Volume: Over 6,800 links were identified, with hundreds viewed by the researchers.
  • Sensitive examples:
    • Marketing company’s revenue review
    • Small‑business owner’s loan application
    • Workplace full‑year staff calendar
    • Notes for a job candidate’s call with an AI lab
  • Meta’s response:

    “However, we’ve paused this functionality while we review this report and consider changes to how these links can be discovered.”

💡 Why it matters

  • The incident highlights how easily AI conversation links can become public when URL design leaks metadata.
  • It joins previous cases where chat exports from OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Anthropic’s Claude, and xAI’s Grok appeared in Google Search, underscoring broader privacy challenges in AI chat sharing features.

#Meta #MuseAI #Privacy

Source: Meta pauses Muse sharing after researchers find AI chats on the web

item.title: Bluesky expands Attie AI tool to create lightweight social apps
item.description:
Bluesky expands Attie AI tool to create lightweight social apps

Bluesky’s Attie AI tool, which launched earlier this year as a way to build your own feeds with AI, now lets users create small social apps – from games to polls – and publish them as individual websites.

🔍 Overview

  • Attie was introduced as a feed‑building AI assistant and is being broadened to support “small” social apps such as games, polls, and dashboards that can be shared with others as their own websites.
  • The tool is positioned by Bluesky as a way to do “social vibe coding or vibe coding for your community.”

🧩 How it works

  • Users create an app simply by typing a natural‑language prompt.
  • The AI generates the functional app in a matter of minutes. For example, “A simple poll I made about Pokémon Red and Pokémon Blue took a few minutes to generate.”

⚙️ Key details

  • Supported app types: games, polls, dashboards, quizzes, idle clickers, and more.

  • Examples highlighted on the Attie site:

    Example Description
    Flappy Butterfly Flappy Bird‑style clone
    Drum machine Simple online drum sequencer
    Quiz Interactive quiz app
    Celery Man idle clicker Idle clicker about a celery man

  • Each example lives on a custom attie.site link with attribution for the creator displayed at the bottom of the page.

  • The apps are described as “pretty lightweight novelties, though I liked the drum machine.”

🚀 Availability

  • Attie apps can be shared instantly as standalone web pages on the attie.site domain.
  • The tool is currently live and can be accessed directly through Bluesky’s platform.

💡 Why it matters

  • By allowing anyone to generate functional mini‑apps with a prompt, Attie lowers the barrier to creating community‑specific tools.
  • Bluesky CEO Toni Schneider framed the vision as “social vibe coding or vibe coding for your community,” emphasizing a shift toward user‑driven, AI‑assisted social experiences.

#Bluesky #Attie #AI #NoCode #SocialApps

Source: Bluesky’s AI tool now lets you make games and apps to share on social

item.title: AI‑Generated Mia Goth Image Spread via Verified Fan Account, Instagram Removes It
item.description:
AI‑Generated Mia Goth Image Spread via Verified Fan Account, Instagram Removes It

An AI‑generated image of actress Mia Goth wearing a T‑shirt that read MY EX IS MY BIGGEST FAN was posted on Instagram shortly after she filed for divorce from Shia LaBeouf. The post quickly went viral and was eventually taken down by the platform.

🔍 Overview

  • The image was created with artificial‑intelligence tools, as reported by The Verge.
  • It featured a Beyoncé song, “Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It),” added to the post.
  • AI photos and videos of celebrities are racking up millions of views on social media.
  • The Instagram account @miagoth_ had more than one million followers and displayed a blue “verified” checkmark.

📲 How the AI Image Gained Traction

  • The post garnered nearly 500,000 likes within days, including likes from peers in the entertainment industry, despite being labelled a fan account.
  • The account had previously been complained to by Goth’s representative for posting “counterfeit, AI images” of her.
  • Meta’s policy allows users to purchase blue verification checkmarks even when the account is not an official page.
  • The news of Goth’s divorce caused the post to be mentioned by celebrity‑gossip outlets, which in turn drove traffic through Google search.
  • Searches for the actress and the shirt produced an AI‑generated overview stating Goth was taking “a clear swipe at her ex, Shia LaBeouf, following their recent divorce filing,” and cited the same blogs.
  • A Google search result section titled “Mia Goth turns heads on Instagram by wearing a sassy ‘My ex is my biggest fan’ t‑shirt” was featured prominently, linking to social‑media discussions of the image.

🛑 Platform Response

  • Instagram eventually removed the @miagoth_ account for impersonating a public figure.
  • Christine Tripicchio, a representative for Goth, said:

    “The fact that this fan account meets Instagram’s criteria to qualify for a ‘blue check’ is disconcerting on a fundamental level.” “Beyond that, it is incomprehensible that Instagram evidently prioritizes the dissemination of forged and manipulated images over the protection and integrity of a public figure’s likeness.”

  • Platform policy statement from Dziedzan:

    “We do not permit accounts to use someone’s likeness to pose as that individual, regardless of whether the content is authentic or AI‑generated.”

💡 Why It Matters

  • The incident highlights how purchased verification can lend credibility to fan or impersonator accounts that circulate deep‑fake content.
  • It demonstrates the rapid amplification of AI‑generated celebrity material through gossip outlets and search engines.
  • The case adds to a growing list of celebrity actions against non‑consensual AI portrayals, such as Scarlett Johansson’s legal team response to an OpenAI voice and Ariana Grande blocking an AI‑content account.
  • Legislative context: the U.S. Take It Down Act (signed in 2025) criminalizes the distribution of non‑consensual intimate imagery, including AI‑generated content, and requires platforms to remove it within 48 hours.
  • Together, these factors underscore the need for clearer verification standards and more aggressive enforcement against unauthorised AI‑generated likenesses.

#AIdeepfakes #InstagramVerification #CelebrityAI #DigitalSafety

Source: Nobody is safe from celebrity AI deepfakes

item.title: AI‑generated Mia Goth image sparks debate over Instagram verification and labeling
item.description:
AI‑generated Mia Goth image sparks debate over Instagram verification and labeling

Earlier this month, an AI‑generated photo of actress Mia Goth wearing a T‑shirt that reads “MY EX IS MY BIGGEST FAN” and set to Beyoncé’s “Single Ladies (Put a Ring on It)” went viral on Instagram. The picture was posted by a fan‑run account (miagoth_) that carried a blue verified checkmark and had over a million followers, causing many to assume it was authentic.

🔍 Overview

  • The post spread across the web and was liked by hundreds of thousands, including people in the entertainment industry.
  • Entertainment outlets such as OK! and People reported on the image as if it were genuine.
  • Goth’s representatives confirmed the image was AI‑generated and that the account had been asked to be removed.

🛡️ Verification & Confusion

  • The miagoth_ account was labeled as fan‑run but displayed a blue checkmark, a symbol that for years signaled an official, authentic entity.
  • Meta’s verification program now allows any account that pays for a blue checkmark to display the badge, even if it is not run by the person depicted in the content.
  • Christine Tripicchio, a representative for Goth, told The Verge: “Mia Goth does not have ownership of, nor does she engage in social media on any platform. We have filed multiple complaints with Instagram to remove the verified fan account which continues to post counterfeit, AI images of Mia Goth.”

⚙️ Platform Response & Policy

  • Meta removed the miagoth_ account, with spokesperson Alex Dziedzan stating it was removed for impersonating a public figure.
  • Rather than ban AI‑generated content of real people, Meta labels some generative‑AI material.
  • Photorealistic AI videos of people may require an AI label, but Meta’s rules carve out an exemption for still images.
  • Meta executives have indicated that AI‑generated content will be a key part of how users engage on the company’s platforms moving forward.

📚 Related Incidents

  • In 2024, Scarlett Johansson said OpenAI used a sound‑alike for the voice of ChatGPT after she declined to work with the company.
  • The same year, Taylor Swift endorsed Kamala Harris for president, saying AI‑generated images of her posted by Donald Trump made her realize she needed to “combat misinformation” around her voting intentions.

💡 Why it matters

  • The blue verification badge can mislead audiences about the provenance of AI‑generated media.
  • The exemption for still images leaves a large gap in the platform’s ability to flag synthetic content that can spread quickly.
  • High‑profile misuse of AI‑generated media underscores growing concerns about misinformation, deepfakes, and the need for clearer labeling standards across social networks.

#AI #Instagram #Verification #Deepfakes

Source: It’s ‘incomprehensible’ that Instagram allowed an AI image of Mia Goth to spread, say her reps

item.title: Meta brings Your Algorithm customization feature to Facebook
item.description:
Meta brings Your Algorithm customization feature to Facebook

Meta is introducing the “Your Algorithm” feature to Facebook, allowing users to directly manage and customize the content they see in their feed and Facebook Reels. This toolset is part of a broader implementation of AI-powered features designed to provide users with more control over their algorithmic recommendations.

🧩 How it works

  • Users can access the feature via the three dots menu on individual posts.
  • You can select “interested” or “not interested” to adjust recommendations.
  • The system may ask follow-up questions to gain more detail on user preferences.
  • You can describe in your own words what content you want to see more or less of.

⚙️ Key details

  • Recommendations respond in real time, adapting within the same session to reflect user input.
  • Meta is increasing the use of Large Language Models (LLMs) in ranking systems to interpret user intent and natural language.
  • The feature has previously launched on Instagram and as “Dear Algo” on Threads.

💡 Why it matters

Meta states that using LLMs allows the algorithm to incorporate interests, context, and intent behind natural language, effectively creating an algorithm that users can talk to.

#Meta #Facebook #ArtificialIntelligence #LLM #Algorithms

Source: Facebook will let you customize your feed algorithm using AI

item.title: Instagram adds AI creative assistant to standalone Edits app
item.description:
Instagram adds AI creative assistant to standalone Edits app

Instagram has announced a new AI-powered “creative assistant” within its standalone Edits app designed to provide creators with feedback and suggestions for their posts.

🧩 How it works

The AI creative assistant analyzes data and metrics from a user’s Instagram account, including:

  • Likes
  • Views
  • Shares
  • Retention on videos

Instagram states that the tool can identify patterns over time to provide suggestions that exceed what metrics alone can offer.

⚙️ Key details

Creators can use the assistant to ask open-ended questions and receive guidance on several areas:

Category AI Assistance Capabilities
Content Analysis Why one video worked and another didn’t, and which content resonated most
Trend Tracking What is trending on Instagram and which audio tracks are trending
Creative Guidance Ideas for content, how to hook viewers, caption suggestions, and video scripting

🚀 Availability

The new feature is free for creators to use up to a certain point. Meta says “power users” have the option to purchase a Meta One subscription for increased usage.

💡 Why it matters

This development follows similar moves by YouTube, which recently updated its AI-powered dashboard (initially announced in 2025) to include A/B testing and AI editing to help creators maximize engagement. While both platforms now offer personalized advice on how to navigate the algorithm, tools like CrowdTangle—previously used by journalists and researchers to monitor popular content on Meta platforms—have been restricted or shut down.

#Instagram #Meta #AI #ContentCreation #SocialMedia

Source: Instagram is adding an AI ‘assistant’ to tell you how to post

item.title: AI Tool Developed to Identify Reply Bots on Bluesky
item.description:
AI Tool Developed to Identify Reply Bots on Bluesky

A new tool has been developed using Opus 5.5 to examine Bluesky profiles for evidence of likely reply bots.

🧩 How it works

The tool analyzes profiles for specific signals to identify bot behavior:

  • Replies posted within seconds of other posts from the same account
  • Accounts that consistently reply to messages from higher-follower users without posting their own content, images, or links
  • The presence of question marks

⚙️ Key details

The development of this tool was made possible because Bluesky has a freely available and useful API, unlike Twitter, where automated reply bots are described as a scourge and have begun manifesting on Bluesky as well.

#Bluesky #Opus5.5 #BotDetection #AI

Source: Tool: Bluesky reply bot checker

item.title: Meta Launches AI Tools for Game Development on Horizon Platform
item.description:
Meta Launches AI Tools for Game Development on Horizon Platform

Meta has announced a plan to encourage game creation for its Horizon social platform through two new AI-powered development tools. This move follows a recent pivot for Horizon, which launched as a VR app but now primarily focuses on mobile.

🧩 How it works

Meta is introducing tools that allow users to create games using AI prompts. According to Meta, these tools enable creators to turn ideas into complete 2D or 3D mobile games that include:

  • Progression systems
  • Balanced difficulty
  • Art direction
  • Multiplayer

⚙️ Key details

Tool Platform Description
Horizon Create Mobile App Create games with AI prompts
Horizon Studio Browser App Create games with AI prompts and more granular controls

To increase the reach of these games, Meta will allow titles made with Horizon Create and Horizon Studio to be recommended and played directly on Facebook and Instagram. Meta states, “Someone scrolling through Instagram can tap a clip of your game and be in a multiplayer session within seconds, without needing to download an app or being redirected.” Games that are “engaging, stable, culturally relevant, and keep players coming back” will receive more reach.

🚀 Availability

The apps will be available in early access, and interested users can sign up for a waitlist.

💡 Why it matters

This push into AI-generated video games comes as Roblox, a similar and more popular platform with 123 million daily active users, is also implementing AI-powered development features in its mobile app. By contrast, Horizon has struggled to gain similar scale, with a 2022 report indicating it had 300,000 monthly users.

#Meta #Horizon #AI #GameDev

Source: Meta is going to let you build games with AI right on your phone

item.title: Meta Launches Meta One Subscription Bundles with Enhanced AI Usage
item.description:
Meta Launches Meta One Subscription Bundles with Enhanced AI Usage

Meta is launching Meta One subscription bundles that pair its standalone app subscriptions with additional AI usage. While some bundles were tested earlier this year, they are now available globally for individual users, creators, and businesses.

🧩 How it works

Meta One bundles integrate subscriptions for Instagram Plus, WhatsApp Plus, and Facebook Plus. These bundles provide “more media generation with Meta AI,” including the use of Instagram’s Restyle and generating images with Muse. Meta states that the “core experience” of Meta AI and its apps will remain free, and standalone subscriptions for Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp will remain available without a bundle.

⚙️ Key details

Individual Plans

Individual bundles start at $7.99 per month and include perks such as a bold follow button and 48-hour Instagram stories. These bundles are a few dollars cheaper than paying $11 per month for all three standalone subscriptions.

Plan Monthly Price Key Features
Core $7.99 Instagram Plus, WhatsApp Plus, Facebook Plus, and increased Meta AI media generation
Premium $19.99 Instagram Plus, WhatsApp Plus, Facebook Plus, and increased Meta AI media generation

Creator and Business Plans

Bundles for creators and businesses range from $14.99 to $499 per month and include a verified badge, higher search result rankings, and monitoring for fake impersonation accounts.

Plan Monthly Price Key Features
Essential $14.99 Verified badge, verified WhatsApp Business channel, impersonation protection, and Meta Business Agent on WhatsApp for 24/7 customer response
Advanced $49.99 Scheduling stories up to 30 days in advance, links in reels and organic posts, exportable analytics, audience insights, team account access, more linked devices, WhatsApp business broadcast credits, and increased Meta Business Agent responses
Expert $149 Highest levels of feature access and Meta Business Agent capacity for scale
Max $499 Highest levels of feature access and Meta Business Agent capacity for scale

🚀 Availability

Meta One bundles are available globally starting today. Meta plans to expand these bundles over time to include AI glasses and “Edits.”

#Meta #MetaAI #Subscription #SocialMedia

Source: Meta’s new One subscriptions put a price on social media and AI

item.title: Meta Changes AI Chatbot Prompt Suggestions After Digging for Personal Information
item.description:
Meta Changes AI Chatbot Prompt Suggestions After Digging for Personal Information

Meta is making changes to the suggested prompts of its AI chatbot following a viral video that showed the assistant seeking personal information about a user’s young daughters.

🔍 Overview

The changes come after Instagram user Kalie Robins posted a video detailing an invasive prompt presented by Meta AI. After cross-posting a video of her and her child singing in a car to Facebook, the prompt “Who is the child passenger?” appeared beneath the clip.

When Robins selected the prompt, Meta AI gathered information about her daughters from her previous posts, as well as posts shared by her relatives. The assistant then:

  • Suggested additional prompts asking about her children’s ages.
  • Suggested prompts asking where Robins lives with her family.
  • Showed photos of her daughters posted to the platform, including one Robins claims she deleted years ago.

⚙️ Key details

In a statement, Meta spokesperson Dina El-Kassaby stated that the company “missed the mark,” adding that “the feature never should have prompted the individual with questions like that.”

El-Kassaby provided several clarifications regarding the incident and the feature’s mechanics:

  • Fix implemented: Meta has resolved the issue causing Meta AI to suggest prompts related to personal topics.
  • Feature intent: The feature was designed to help users obtain more information about topics or posts that interest them.
  • Information access: When a user clicks a prompt, the generated response is based entirely on information the user already has access to. In this specific case, El-Kassaby noted that Meta AI may have pulled from videos where Robins named her children.

🌐 Context and Integration

Meta has integrated its AI assistant across its primary platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger, where it can answer questions, write posts, and generate images. This is not the first time Meta has adjusted its AI features due to user response; in July, the company pulled a feature that allowed users to create AI deepfakes of other Instagram users after facing fierce backlash.

#MetaAI #Privacy #SocialMedia #ArtificialIntelligence

Source: Meta says it’s changing AI suggestions after posing invasive personal questions
